title: Subcanonical clusters and the splitting index of their section space
statement: Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume $X$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes, meaning that at every singular closed point its completed local $k$-algebra is $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Write $h^i(X,F)=\dim_kH^i(X,F)$ for Zariski module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Let $T\subseteq X$ be a zero-dimensional closed subscheme, possibly empty, with ideal $I_T$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], and let $\omega_X$ be the dualizing invertible module [lem-sfb-nodal-line-serre-riemann-roch]. Say that $T$ is subcanonical if $F=I_T\otimes\omega_X$ has a global section nonzero at every irreducible-component generic point [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-irreducible-components]. Put $V=H^0(X,F)$, regarded as a subspace of $H^0(X,\omega_X)$ through the ideal inclusion. For a reduced union $A$ of components put $V_A=\{s\in V:s_\eta=0\text{ for every component generic point }\eta\notin A\}$. A partition $\mathcal P$ of the finite set of irreducible components is admissible if the summation map $\bigoplus_{A\in\mathcal P}V_A\to V$ is an isomorphism, each block denoting its reduced union. For $T\ne\varnothing$, define the splitting index $r(T)$ as the largest integer $|\mathcal P|-1$ over admissible partitions. The one-block partition is admissible and there are finitely many partitions, so this specifies an integer $r(T)\ge0$. For the empty cluster set $r(\varnothing)=0$, by convention, regardless of the admissible partitions of its section space.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q80-fde31563e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I checked the source myself: I fetched the author-hosted Franciosi–Tenni PDF into /tmp and read the text, because the local copy is WANTED. The only real change is to the statement: r(T) is still the largest |P|-1 over admissible partitions when T is nonempty, and r(∅)=0 is now set explicitly. Def. 2.16 (p.233) says exactly this: 'We define the splitting index of the zero cluster to be zero', and Def. 2.3 calls the empty set the degree-0 cluster. Def. 2.16 literally says 'minimal number k', which is a misprint; the finest decomposition used in Prop. 2.17(i) is what the definition means, and it equals the maximum here because the common refinement of two admissible partitions is admissible on a reduced curve. The worker's counterexample is correct: on two elliptic curves meeting at one node, H^0(ω) is the direct sum of the two component pieces (by the residue theorem), so the old definition gave r(∅)=1 where the source gives 0. stmt_deps, source, blueprint, created and unit are unchanged; all 13 stmt_deps were read and say what is used; no new nodes; the searches are recorded; no SGA. Only two nodes cite this one. lem-sfb-subcanonical-splitting-clifford-bound for T=∅ becomes h^0(ω) ≤ p_a, which is true and matches F–T Thm 3.7. Maintainer note: step 2 of lem-sfb-nodal-two-connected-clifford claims 'r(T̄)=r', which would need the empty case handled. That case cannot happen under the lemma's hypotheses: 2-connected and not P^1 makes |K| base-point free (F–T Thm 2.5(ii)), so b=0 and T̄=∅. Also, the step's partition argument works unchanged with r:=r(T̄). Its statement and proof stand; only the wording should mention the empty case. No fixes.
